narrative_summary: Global geopolitics, domestic governance, and the tech sector are experiencing profound shifts driven by high-stakes diplomacy, leadership crises, and massive capital movements. A trilateral summit in Shenzhen featuring Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin, and Xi Jinping yielded a Kremlin-published agreement that elevates authoritarian interests and advances energy cooperation to bolster Russia's war economy. Concurrently, the artificial intelligence sector reached a monumental milestone as Anthropic launched a historic $81 billion initial public offering, valuing the company at $1.5 trillion and underscoring the deep reliance of the broader economy on a handful of tech giants. This corporate dominance mirrors anxieties expressed across public institutions, where regulatory failures, political polarization, and systemic accountability gaps challenge both democratic norms and economic stability.

source_summaries.title: John Fetterman’s Days Seem Numbered—and He Knows It
bullets: Sen. John Fetterman's recent political behavior, including appealing to Republican donors and criticizing fellow Democrats, has effectively provoked a potential primary challenge.
House Democrats and politicians in Pennsylvania are actively considering mounting primary challenges against Fetterman for his Senate seat in 2028.

source_summaries.title: Patrick Gaspard: We Have to Keep the New Electoral Map
bullets: The pro-democracy coalition must maintain the electoral territory it gained in the midterms to defeat the MAGA movement.
Sustaining these political gains requires engaged candidates who productively collaborate with corporate America for community benefit.
Additional priorities for Democrats include maintaining a moral stance on immigration and rethinking primary debates for 2028.

source_summaries.title: The Two Biggest Rats Are Jumping Ship
bullets: Elon Musk claimed in an interview that he is a political moderate who supports divided government and is not affiliated with the MAGA movement, despite having spent hundreds of millions of dollars backing Republican candidates.
JD Vance subtly distanced himself from Donald Trump during an interview by attributing decisions regarding Iran to Trump alone and setting a strict timeline for ending the military involvement.

source_summaries.title: Elon Musk Spent $700 Million on MAGA. Now He’s Having Regrets
bullets: Elon Musk has told The New York Times that he is not MAGA and regrets a portion of the $700 million he spent electing Republicans and supporting Donald Trump's agenda.
Analysts view Musk's sudden distancing from the movement as damage control rather than a genuine shift in his personal convictions.
Musk's heavy political involvement has resulted in significant backlash, damaging Tesla's brand and harming his public image.

source_summaries.title: A Military Deal With Venezuela Is the Easy Part
bullets: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth traveled to Caracas and announced a new U.S.-Venezuela agreement focused on military training, intelligence sharing, and border security.
The deal follows the U.S. capture of former Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro, though much of the pre-existing political and military establishment remains in power.
While security cooperation is a standard component of U.S. strategy, building lasting partnerships requires years of sustained diplomatic and military effort.

source_summaries.title: The Worst Throuple on the Planet
bullets: Elon Musk expressed regret over his massive political spending after failing to secure desired outcomes in recent midterm elections.
Donald Trump, Xi Jinping, and Vladimir Putin participated in a trilateral meeting in Shenzhen that elevated Putin on the world stage.
The summit in Shenzhen raises concerns among critics about the symbolic degradation of American leadership and democratic values.

source_summaries.title: How to fight monopoly
bullets: Hollywood has become significantly more concentrated following Skydance's acquisition of both Paramount and Warner Bros.
Despite increased industry consolidation, the movie industry is experiencing its healthiest post-pandemic box office year yet.
Monopoly threats in the film sector remain low because First Amendment protections and low production costs keep barriers to entry minimal.

source_summaries.title: “The Argument” podcast, ad free: Why is Gen Z so mad?
bullets: Young people today perceive the current economic climate as historically poor despite standard indicators.
Economics commentator Kyla Scanlon joined "The Argument" podcast to analyze why Generation Z feels this way.

source_summaries.title: NASDAQ: ANT
bullets: Anthropic's upcoming IPO will provide crucial insights into the future trajectory of the broader artificial intelligence market.
The Prof G newsletter is transitioning its Extra Credit feature to a weekly schedule covering deep-dive business topics.
Upcoming media coverage will analyze Anthropic's S-1 filing, data center compute futures, and AI integration in storytelling.

source_summaries.title: REPLAY: Trump’s Autocrat Playdate with Xi and Putin Produced Zero Results
bullets: Scott Galloway and Jessica Tarlov discussed Donald Trump's summit with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin, which yielded no substantial results.
Anthropic made its historic stock market debut while Jensen Huang faced a corporate petition to reinstate him at Nvidia.
Hakeem Jeffries secured the Democratic nomination for Speaker of the House, positioning himself to become the first Black Speaker in U.S. history.

source_summaries.title: REPLAY: The Nvidia Scandal — with Aswath Damodaran
bullets: An unedited replay of a conversation between Ed and Aswath Damodaran regarding Nvidia and Anthropic is available exclusively for Prof G+ subscribers.
A condensed version of the discussion will be published on the Prof G Markets feed.

source_summaries.title: Anthropic’s $1.5 Trillion IPO Is A Trap
bullets: Ed Elson and Paul Kedrosky discuss Anthropic's anticipated IPO, trading trajectory, and the Nvidia scandal.
Joost van Dreunen analyzes the release of Grand Theft Auto VI and its critical impact on the broader gaming industry.
The program concludes with a review of New York's pied-a-terre tax.

source_summaries.title: Thrilling.
bullets: A twice-yearly injection called diranersen halved the rate of cognitive decline in Alzheimer's patients and reduced tau protein tangles in a major trial.
Pew Research Center projections indicate that Muslims are expected to outnumber Christians globally by 2035.
Anthropic is valued at approximately $1.5 trillion and will begin trading on Nasdaq following a record $81 billion initial public offering.

source_summaries.title: The U.S. Paid Insurers Billions to Cover Civilians Harmed in War. Even the Government Says the System Is Ripe for Fraud.
bullets: A federal workers' compensation program for contractors injured in war zones has paid nearly $5 billion to insurance companies over the past decade, with internal memos describing the system as ripe for fraud.
The Labor Department has failed to properly police the program due to lacking oversight, dysfunctional technology, and an inability to prevent excessive or unreasonable insurance payments.
Insurers have exploited the system by rapidly settling dubious claims to collect government reimbursements or by fighting legitimate claims before ultimately billing taxpayers.

source_summaries.title: Corpus Christi Started Pumping Groundwater at “Lightning Speed.” Rural Residents Fear the Consequences.
bullets: Corpus Christi rapidly drilled wells into a regional aquifer to combat drought, alarming rural residents who feared losing their water access.
The city utilized a local conservation district staffed by city employees and overseen by city-appointed officials to fast-track and approve all its drilling permits.
Despite studies warning that the pumping could cause land to sink and water levels to drop, the district authorized the city to pump up to 40 million gallons daily.

source_summaries.title: The Trump DOJ Quietly Intervened to Ink a Huge Payout to a Trump Golf Pro
bullets: Top Trump administration officials intervened to help a Trump golf club pro and a media-connected company secure unusually large half-million-dollar payouts from the IRS.
The settlement amount is 250 times higher than statutory limits without standard IRS legal consultations, prompting legal experts to question its legitimacy.
The agreement has raised concerns that it could serve as a backdoor method to fund payouts for Trump's inner circle following the collapse of a previous DOJ settlement proposal.

source_summaries.title: We’re Publishing the Tariff Refunds the Government Has Refused to Disclose
bullets: ProPublica published a database detailing over $28 billion in tariff refunds recovered or expected by 343 publicly traded companies following the Supreme Court's February 2026 ruling.
U.S. Customs and Border Protection refused to publicly disclose which companies are receiving the roughly $170 billion in total refunds or the amounts requested.
At least nine companies have disclosed plans to use their tariff refunds for bonuses rather than reimbursing consumers who bore the cost through higher prices.

source_summaries.title: See How Much Companies Are Getting in Tariff Refunds
bullets: ProPublica released a database titled "Cash Back" detailing tariff refunds under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act.
The data covers 343 public companies that have recovered or expect to receive refunds.
The total amount of these tariff refunds exceeds $28 billion.

source_summaries.title: These Teachers Were Charged With Sexual Abuse. California Could Have Revoked Their Licenses Earlier but Didn’t.
bullets: California's educator licensing agency failed to investigate or revoke the credentials of teachers reported for sexual abuse, allowing them to continue working at multiple schools.
State investigators omitted interviews with several students who alleged abuse, and panels occasionally overlooked evidence of wrongdoing.
Accused elementary school counselor David Braff and two other convicted teachers retained their licenses until their criminal arrests years after schools initially reported them.

source_summaries.title: Calls for court packing fail the test of history
bullets: Prominent Democrats have increasingly called to expand the Supreme Court to 13 justices to match the number of federal circuits.
Proponents argue for a one-to-one ratio between justices and circuits, but this justification is pretextual because circuit-riding ended over a century ago.
Historical changes to the court's size addressed practical administrative needs rather than partisan control, unlike current court-packing proposals.

source_summaries.title: The Supreme Court and congressional investigations
bullets: The Trump administration asked the Supreme Court to block a ruling that maintained the Temporary Protected Status program for Venezuelan nationals.
The Supreme Court's December argument session is scheduled to begin on Monday, November 30.

source_summaries.title: Kremlin Reveals Trump-Putin-Xi Summit Document: What Russia, China and US Agreed On
bullets: The Kremlin published a four-point agreement following a trilateral summit between Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin, and Xi Jinping covering UN reform, energy cooperation, international criminal justice, and nuclear security.
The proposed UN reform calls for strengthening international security while omitting any limits on the veto powers held by Russia, China, and the United States.
The leaders agreed to increase energy production and market stability, which directly benefits Russia's war economy despite existing Western sanctions.

The document emphasizes state sovereignty and official immunity to prevent the International Criminal Court from exercising its powers, which is particularly beneficial for Putin due to his existing arrest warrant.

source_summaries.title: It’s Wrong to Give Leaders a Pass for Wrongdoing
bullets: The CEO of the world's most valuable company recently resigned following confessions of affairs with subordinates and a suspected Chinese spy.
Research utilizing leaked Ashley Madison data demonstrates that individuals who cheat on their romantic partners are statistically more likely to commit professional misconduct.
Traits like opportunism, entitlement, and greed transcend personal lives, showing that personal integrity and professional behavior are deeply connected.

source_summaries.source: Heather Cox Richardson from Letters from an American
source_summaries.title: The Gettysburg Address
bullets: The publication is an edition of Letters from an American by Heather Cox Richardson titled The Gettysburg Address.
The content primarily consists of subscription prompts, listening links, and social media directories rather than substantive article text.

source_summaries.title: A(nother) small win and a big thank you!!
bullets: Louis-François from What's AI announced reaching a milestone of 43 paid subscribers.
The author expressed gratitude to both paid and free subscribers for supporting the newsletter's mission to make AI accessible.
Work is underway on finishing the upcoming book, AI Engineering for Production, which will be provided as a free ebook to paid subscribers.

source_summaries.title: Sanctions and Other Consolations
bullets: Politicians frequently favor economic sanctions because they create the appearance of toughness at minimal domestic cost.
Historical records and academic research demonstrate that economic sanctions rarely achieve their intended goals.
Economic theory indicates that sanctions fail largely because authoritarian rulers managed to avoid bearing the true costs.

source_summaries.title: How The Merely Rich Wield Power In The Age Of Billionaires
bullets: Economists Owen Zidar and Eric Zwick argue that focusing solely on outlier tech billionaires distorts our understanding of American wealth and political influence.
A significant portion of America's wealth is generated by mundane local enterprises such as car dealerships, dental offices, and construction firms.
Owners of these widespread, mid-tier businesses collectively wield enormous influence over taxes, regulations, and the economy.

source_summaries.title: AVDD Strait of Hormuz SITREP
bullets: Gulf crude oil exports have partially recovered to prewar levels despite ongoing attacks on commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.
Saudi-Houthi hostilities have intensified, marked by a Houthi missile strike that damaged a major tower in Riyadh.
The International Energy Agency characterizes the ongoing conflict as the largest energy supply shock in history.

source_summaries.title: The Summit Failed — Why Trump and Putin Won’t Quit
bullets: The recent Shenzhen summit failed to address critical issues regarding the wars in Ukraine and Iran, resulting in a peace declaration that omitted key conflicts.
Leaders like Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin refuse to quit their respective losing conflicts because exiting without a deal guarantees immediate political ruin.
Both leaders are instead choosing to escalate their military engagements, mirroring historical precedents like Lyndon Johnson's actions in Vietnam.

source_summaries.title: Weekly Briefing: 200,000+ People Call for Jensen Huang’s Return, Microsoft 365 Goes Down, & the Fed Warns AI Could…
bullets: Over 200,000 supporters and employees petitioned for Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia's CEO, though the board unanimously rejected the campaign.
A global Microsoft 365 outage highlighted the heavy reliance of modern organizations on a limited number of technology infrastructure providers.
The Federal Reserve warned that artificial intelligence productivity gains and labor impacts could disproportionately affect younger workers.

source_summaries.title: Sabato's Crystal Ball - Americans Want AI Rules, But Aren't Sure They Would Work - Vol. 24, Iss. 89
bullets: Majorities of Americans favor proposed artificial intelligence regulations, but a smaller share believes those rules would actually be effective.
Citizens express more trust in specific duties, such as mandatory human oversight or content labels, than in the creation of new institutions or regulatory agencies.
Republicans and Democrats largely agree on supporting AI rules, though Republicans show slightly higher confidence in their effectiveness.

source_summaries.title: LAI #152: Is Your Agent Failing Outside the Model?
bullets: Agent failures are frequently caused by surrounding system issues like missing tools, context compaction, and data-pipeline controls rather than the underlying model.
The publication explores harness design, tool selection strategies, and JEPA world models to improve agent reliability and performance.
A practical tip for reducing hallucinations involves asking models to provide word-for-word quotes supporting their claims or replacing unsupported statements with brackets.

source_summaries.title: Data Science Weekly - Issue 678
bullets: Data Science Weekly Issue 678 features curated news, articles, and jobs related to data science, AI, and machine learning.

Featured topics include an algorithmic analysis of SimCity source code, an interactive app demonstrating Bayesian updating, and the emergence of the Data Intelligence Engineer role in AI-enabled teams.

source_summaries.title: Poll: No clear leader in 2028 Democratic primary; Rubio leads Vance for GOP nod
bullets: A November 2026 poll indicates that the 2028 Democratic primary race currently has no clear leader, with nearly half of Democratic voters unable to name a preferred candidate in an open-text prompt.
Democratic voters express a desire for candidates who are young, authentic, and strong on the economy.
Marco Rubio holds a slim lead over JD Vance and Ron DeSantis for the 2028 Republican nomination.

source_summaries.title: A Bridge, I Mean Post, Too Far
bullets: Paul Krugman was unable to write a full article because he was keynoting at the IMF's Statistical Forum.
He mentioned taking Amtrak to Washington, D.C., where he observed a passenger watching his video discussion with Heather Cox Richardson.
He provided a link to the official video and transcript from the CUNY Graduate Center.

source_summaries.title: The National Popular Vote Plan, explained
bullets: Recent state-level Democratic victories have renewed interest in passing the National Popular Vote Plan.
The NPVP is an interstate compact designed to ensure the winner of the national popular vote secures the presidency.
Advocates argue the plan prevents outcomes where a candidate wins the White House despite receiving fewer popular votes nationwide.

source_summaries.source: Michael Spencer and Michael Fritzell from AI Supremacy
source_summaries.title: ANT, the IPO of the Century
bullets: Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 per share, aiming to raise roughly $94.48 billion in gross proceeds.
Founded by former OpenAI talent, Anthropic and OpenAI have collectively raised $428.4 billion, accounting for about 27 percent of all startup AI funding over five years.
Alphabet and Amazon hold a combined 28 percent equity stake in Anthropic, tied closely to cloud computing and TPU incentives.

source_summaries.title: The Authoritarian Economy
bullets: Jensen Huang stated he would return as Nvidia CEO if requested by the board following his resignation amid a controversy involving intelligence agency allegations.
Robert Reich argues that the American economy has shifted from a democratic model toward an authoritarian one controlled by a handful of powerful tech executives.
Nvidia's recent market volatility highlights how the broader AI industry and the economy have become dangerously dependent on single corporate leaders considered too big to fail.

publications: Michael Spencer and Michael Fritzell from AI Supremacy
Heather Cox Richardson from Letters from an American
